programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Dan & Gran
programme.desc: Stan and Gran get the giggles while spotting nature on the Ley, and the lake seems to be giggling back at them! Who is that laughing? Tha Dan is Gran a' cireasail fhad 's a tha 'd a' coimhead nàdar air an Loch, 's tha 'n Loch mar gu bheil e a' cireasail air ais thuca! Cò tha siud a' gàireachdaich?

programme.title: Beathaichean a’ Bocadaich
programme.desc: Tha Sophie a’ coimhead tron phrosbaig sheunta aice airson faicinn ciamar a bhios beathaichean a’ bocadaich. Tha i ag ionnsachadh mar a bhios diofar bheathaichean a’ gluasad agus cuide ri a caraidean, tha i a’ cruthachadh dannsa. An-diugh, danns coltach ri iasg agus goiriola! Sophie looks through her magic binoculars to find out how animals boogie. She learns how different animals dance and, along with her friends, creates a dance using animal movements. Join her and dance like a fish and a gorilla!

programme.title: Losgannan | Froglets
programme.desc: Cuiridh Ailig suas teanta agus thèid na Losgannan don fhàsach a rannsachadh phioramaidean. When Alex sets up a tent, the Froglets head into the desert as ancient pyramid explorers.

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Tha ’ad uile trang a’ deànamh na rudan air a bheil iad math, ach Beag Chlangair a-mhàin - chan eil coltas ro thrang aireasan. Tha Beag air cuir roimhe rudeigin air a bheil e math a dhèanamh cuideachd. Everyone is busy doing what they’re good at except for Beag Chlangai, he doesn’t appear to be too busy. Beag has also decided he would like to try to do something he’s good at.

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Seach g’eil a h-uile duine nan cadal, tha na slamain airson rùrachadh - is carson a rùraicheadh dithis nuair a dh’fhaodar rùrach le ceathrar! As everyone is asleep the Blobs want to explore and why venture with two, when you can explore…with four!

programme.title: ’S E Iasg a Th’Annam (I’m a Fish)
programme.desc: Tha sinn a' cluinntinn an-diugh cho romansach ’s a tha na capaill-mhara – mar a bhios iad a' tuiteam ann an gaol agus mar bhios iad a' dannsa còmhla. We hear how romantic seahorses are – how they fall in love and dance together.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Mairi NicAonghais a’ leughadh Nansaidh Leòmach. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Jane O’Connor agus a dhealbhachadh le Robin Preiss Glasser. Chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Jo NicDhòmhnaill. A bedtime story for young children. Mairi MacInnes reads Nansaidh Leòmach by Jane O’Connor, illustrated by Robin Preiss Glasser and translated into Gaelic by Jo Macdonald.

programme.title: Clann Na Cruinne
programme.desc: Tha Lan na sgìthear saor-stoidhleach ach feumaidh e ròghnachadh an e cur-seachad proifeiseanta a th’ ann neo nach e. 'S e amas am bliadhna an co-fharpais nàiseanta a bhuannachadh. Lan is a free-style skier but he must decide if he wants it to be a professional pastime or not. His ambition this year is to win the national competition.

programme.title: Belle and Sebastian
programme.desc: Tha trioblaid aig Angelina oir tha cion luchd-turais a' ciallachadh nach eil mòran a’ ceannach an càis aice. Tha i feumach air cuideachadh. ’S math g’ eil Belle is Sebastian deiseil is deònach. Angelina has a problem as a lack of tourists mean that there aren't many people buying her cheese. She needs help. It’s a good thing that Belle and Sebastian are ready and willing.

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Nuair a lorgas an tuathanach gu bheil pìoban ag aoidion, tha e a' cur fios air a' Bhòrd Uisge. Ach fiùs am measg nan duilgheadasan a tha seo, tha an treud a' faicinn cothrom airson beagan fealla-dha! When the farmer discovers he's sprung a leak, he calls the water board to come and fix the problem. The bored flock are thrilled by the opportunity to have some watery fun. When the workmen clock off, the party begins!

programme.title: A’ Chùil
programme.desc: Tha Choirstaidh air ais le prògram eile bhon stiùidio aice, A’ Chùil. Sa phrògram seo tha i a’ dèanamh soidhne agus rudan eile a-mach à sreang airson an stiùidio aice a sgeadachadh. Choirstaidh is back with another programme from her studio A’ Chùil. She makes a sign, and other things, out of string to decorate her studio.

programme.title: An Sgoil
programme.desc: Latha mòr dha Mgr Mackle le Mèar a’ bhaile a’ tighinn airson seann chlach na sgoile a chomharrachadh. Tha Daisy agus Danny trang a’ feuchainn ris a h-uile càil a chur air dòigh ach chan eil Mrs Fullerton neo na faoileagan a' cuideachadh ghnothaichean. A big day for Mr Mackle with the mayor coming to celebrate the school's ancient stone. Daisy and Danny are busy making sure that everything is in place, but Mrs Fullerton and the seagulls aren’t helping matters.

programme.title: Fuine
programme.desc: Gregor samples a new take on custard creams. Griogar MacLeòid is eileanaich eile lem molaidhean son fuine bhlasta staigh agaibh pfhèin.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Calum Maclean is in Fort William visiting an unexpected industrial site.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Rùm Gu Rùm, Le Erica
programme.desc: Tha an cleasaiche, a tha a-nis na dealbhaiche cruthachail thaighean, Erica Mhoireasdan, a’ gabhail sgrìob tron Ghàidhealtachd ‘s na h-Eileanan. Le taic bho luchd-ciùird, tha i a’ lorg dhòighean ùra air seann rumanan a thoirt beò. Actress-turned-interior designer, Erica Morrison, takes us on a design adventure throughout the Highlands and Islands. With the help of local craft workers, she finds new ideas for designing old spaces. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: An t-Eilean/The Island
programme.desc: When Lady Mary Maclean is murdered on the Isle of Harris, newly qualified family liaison officer PC Kat Crichton is assigned to the case. A high-profile case like this is the career opportunity of a lifetime but for Kat, this is not just a job. A decade earlier, she got caught up in the twisted web of the Maclean family and was forced to flee the island. Ten years older, a resolute Kat now returns, determined to bring the killer to justice. Nuair a tha Lady Mary NicIllEathain air a murt sna Hearadh, tha an t-Oifigear Teaghlaich ùr, PC Kat Crichton, a’ tòiseachadh air a’ chùis. Cha ghabh cùis le ìomhaigh cho àrd ri seo a sheachnadh ach do Kat, chan e obair a-mhàin a tha seo. Deich bliadhna roimhe, chaidh a glacadh ann an lìon toinnte teaghlach MhicIllEathain agus b’ fheudar dhi an t-eilean fhàgail. Tha Kat a’ tilleadh, nas sine, dàna agus daingeann gum faigh ceartas làmh an uachdair air a’ mhurtair. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Abigail
programme.desc: Tha an Dutch Baby annasach ach anabarrach blasta. Brunch sònraichte air nach dìochuimhnich thu a’ chiad ghreis. The unusual but extremely delicious Dutch baby is a special brunch that you won't forget in a hurry. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Dàna | Scotland's Wild Side
programme.desc: Tha Coinneach MacFhraing a’ siubhal gu ruige Gleann Nibheis. Tha e a’ dol a shreap sgeir air a bheil ‘Storm’. Tha ‘Storm’ air a fùcadh am meadhan Poll Dubh, fear dheth na h-àiteachan is ainmeil ann an saoghal sreap. Bithidh e mar fhiachaibh air na sgilean a dh’ionnsaich e thar nam bliadhnaichean a chuir gu feum agus cuideachadh fhaighinn bho dheagh charaid. Coinneach MacFhraing travels to Glen Nevis to take on a climb called ‘Storm’, a classic test piece nestled in the middle of Polldubh, one of Scotland’s premier rock-climbing destinations. To succeed, he’ll need to put years of practise to the test and enlist the help of a good friend. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Na Sgiobairean mu Dheireadh/The Last Captains
programme.desc: Tha sealg a’ ghiomaich a’ gluasad chun chladach, agus tha am mì-rian ga leantainn. Ròpaichean air an rocladh, droch nàdar a’ tighinn am bàrr, agus Steven a’ strì gus faighinn dhachaigh ann an tìde airson co-là-breith a mhic. The lobster chase moves inshore - and with it, the chaos. Tangles mount, tempers flare, and Steven races to escape the mess in time for his son’s birthday. Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Rurachd (Foraging)
programme.desc: Mary Ann Kennedy and Lucy Cooke forage at the shore for razor clams, kelp lasagne and carrageen dessert.

programme.title: Transatlantic Sessions
programme.desc: Julie Fowlis agus Muireann Nic Amhlaoibh le taghadh ciùil bho Transatlantic Sessions. Julie Fowlis and Muireann Nic Amhlaoibh present highlights from Transatlantic Sessions.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Beautiful Equations
programme.desc: Artist and writer Matt Collings takes the plunge into an alien world of equations. He asks top scientists to help him understand five of the most famous equations in science, talks to Stephen Hawking about his equation for black holes and comes face to face with a particle of anti-matter. Along the way he discovers why Newton was right about those falling apples and how to make sense of E=mc2. As he gets to grips with these equations he wonders whether the concept of artistic beauty has any relevance to the world of physics.

programme.title: The Flying Gardener
programme.desc: Chris Beardshaw follows in the footsteps of the Scottish adventurers who travelled the globe and risked their lives to bring back plants that are now taken for granted.

programme.title: Ardal O’Hanlon: Tomb Raider
programme.desc: The story of an epic 1930s quest to find the origins of the earliest Irish men and women on the island of Ireland using archaeology. Ardal goes back to world-famous archaeological sites to see how Ireland had some of the most important finds in Europe at the time. Further beneath the surface, Ardal discovers how both in Northern Ireland and what was then called the Irish Free State, archaeology was being used as an important tool for nation-building, as both states forged new identities in the wake of Partition. He unravels a forgotten time period, when a team of Americans from Harvard University, a Nazi archaeologist from Austria and a Welsh geography professor based in Belfast dug up ancient sites across the country. Their pioneering work laid the foundation for modern archaeology in Ireland, north and south, and yet is largely a forgotten story. Through Ardal’s journey, the film rediscovers this strange 1930s tale but also ends up answering some of Ardal’s deepest questions about the Celts, and ultimately, what it means to be Irish.

programme.title: This is BBC Four
programme.desc: Programmes start at 7.00pm.

programme.title: Villages by the Sea
programme.desc: Ben Robinson visits Culross, a stunning example of a 17th-century Scottish royal burgh village. Culross was a major centre for Scottish coal mining and boasts the very first place in the world to have a mine shaft that extended under the sea floor. Entering this village is like stepping back in time 400 years, with many of the interesting details and decorations of the buildings remaining. It is also a place where witch hunting was rife and superstitions lived alongside innovative industry.

programme.title: Wainwright Walks
programme.desc: Julia Bradbury is in Britain's wettest vale, the Borrowdale Valley, to climb to the summit of Castle Crag. Of all 214 fells in Wainwright's pictorial guides, Castle Crag is the only one under 1,000ft to be included. Bradbury's goal is to determine what makes it worthy of such an honour.

programme.title: Treasures of Ancient Rome
programme.desc: In the third and final part of the series, Alastair Sooke charts the decline and fall of the Roman Empire through some of its hidden and most magical artistic treasures. He travels to Leptis Magna in Libya shortly after the overthrow of Gaddafi and finds one of the best preserved Roman cities in the world and the cradle of later Roman art. Sooke discovers glorious mosaics which have never been filmed before, but also finds evidence of shocking neglect of Libya's Roman heritage by the Gaddafi regime. His artistic tour takes him to Egypt and the northern frontiers of the empire where he encounters stunning mummy paintings and exquisite silver and glassware. As Rome careered from one crisis to another, official art became more hard boiled and militaristic and an obscure cult called Christianity rose up to seize the mantle of Western art for centuries to come.

programme.title: Mary Beard's Ultimate Rome: Empire Without Limit
programme.desc: In the second episode, Mary Beard explores the physical world of the Roman Empire, and finds surprising parallels with our own world. Setting out in the footsteps of the emperor Hadrian, she discovers a vast empire bound together by a common material culture, and a globalised economy of such scale that evidence of its side-effects can still be seen today, thousands of miles away from Rome. Mary unpicks the threads of a huge commercial and cultural network, taking in the vital supply of olive oil to Rome and her armies, the slave trade, and the all-important silver mines of Spain. Following the famous Roman road network, and the shipping routes connecting the empire's thriving ports, Mary reveals another side to the Roman Empire, one where builders and traders eclipse soldiers, and starring slaves, not senators, making the most of a hugely connected new world.

programme.title: I, Claudius
programme.desc: As Augustus learned of Livia's plot against Postumus, she took action which resulted in Tiberius becoming emperor. The situation in the east now threatens Tiberius's position.

programme.title: I, Claudius
programme.desc: Germanicus has been murdered in Antioch, and his wife Agrippina is convinced Tiberius ordered the killing. Livia has discovered that Caligula helped to poison his father. While Tiberius's perversions have become notorious, his right-hand man Sejanus, commander of the Praetorian Guard, gathers more power for himself, including a marriage alliance with Claudius.

programme.title: Inside the Bat Cave
programme.desc: A remarkable journey into the secret world of one of the most endangered and least understood animals on earth – bats. Witness the birth of a new generation of pups and follow their progress towards their perilous maiden flight outside the roost.

programme.title: Talking Business
programme.desc: Can oil really save Venezuela's economy? The country has the world's largest reserves, so can it take advantage whilst global energy supplies are under pressure because of events in the Middle East? Reviving Venezuela's biggest industry is just one part of the change that's needed as the country recovers from deadly earthquakes and tries to restructure a mountain of debt after years of mismanagement. Respected former central bank president Ruth Krivoy and leading oil executive Ali Moshiri of Amos Global Energy give their takes on the role oil can play. Meanwhile, the president of Venezuela's Chambers of Commerce and Industry, Felipe Capozzolo of Fedecamaras, explains some of the other reforms that could help the country become wealthy again.

programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: An exciting new species is on its way to the park, but are the keepers ready for these ferocious predators? And can Hamza Yassin uncover a lorikeet love match in the aviary?

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Tracker Shaquille is hot on the heels of a car that could soon be smuggled out of the country and shipped to Romania. The car’s driver has suspected links to an eastern European gang of car thieves, and Shaquille is desperate to get the vehicle back before it disappears for good. With the clock ticking, he traces the car to an address in Warrington – but can he get the driver to hand over the keys? In Birmingham, tracker Neil is closing in on a stolen Audi A4. With a police response vehicle just moments away, the thieves are running out of options. They’re forced to abandon the vehicle and make their getaway on foot. Just a few miles away in Sutton Coldfield, the owner of a VW Golf becomes the latest victim of a trend known as car cannibalism. Thieves cashing in on a shortage of car parts have stripped the entire front end of his vehicle, removing items such as the bonnet, front grill, headlights and bumper. Meanwhile, in Guildford, tracker Richard is searching for a digger that’s been hidden on the edge of a golf course.

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: World silver medallist Amy Hunt is among the favourites for the European 200m title as qualifying gets underway on day 3 of the European Championships in Birmingham. 2025 world indoor champion Amber Anning is hoping to make her comeback from injury to line up in the heats of the 400m. And the men’s decathlon begins with the 100m, the first of ten events over the next two days. Jeanette Kwakye is joined by Jessica Ennis-Hill and Greg Rutherford in the studio, with commentary from Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe.

programme.desc: Like a record, baby! Upcycler Sarah's challenge is to give a dated bureau a bold new look, while blacksmith Kev has a heap of metal chair frames to rework into something spectacular.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A retired army couple looking to escape busy Bedfordshire enlist Margherita Taylor to help them spend their house hunting budget of £680,000 in the rural wilds of Norfolk. programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: Day 3 of the European Athletics Championships draws to a close in Birmingham with local boy Matt Hudson-Smith aiming to become the most successful European male athlete in history in the men’s 400m. Fresh from winning under-23 gold last season, Emily Newnham could be the one to watch in the women’s 400m hurdles final. Medals will also be decided in the men’s discus, the women’s hammer and the men’s sprint hurdles. Gabby Logan leads the coverage and is joined in the studio by Jessica Ennis-Hill, Jenny Meadows and Greg Rutherford, with Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe in commentary.

programme.title: UEFA Champions League
programme.desc: Europa League winners Aston Villa take on Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain in the UEFA Super Cup in Salzburg. PSG are the current holders after coming from 2-0 down to secure victory over Tottenham on penalties last year.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Tracker Shaquille is hot on the heels of a car that could soon be smuggled out of the country and shipped to Romania. The car’s driver has suspected links to an eastern European gang of car thieves, and Shaquille is desperate to get the vehicle back before it disappears for good. With the clock ticking, he traces the car to an address in Warrington – but can he get the driver to hand over the keys? In Birmingham, tracker Neil is closing in on a stolen Audi A4. With a police response vehicle just moments away, the thieves are running out of options. They’re forced to abandon the vehicle and make their getaway on foot. Just a few miles away in Sutton Coldfield, the owner of a VW Golf becomes the latest victim of a trend known as car cannibalism. Thieves cashing in on a shortage of car parts have stripped the entire front end of his vehicle, removing items such as the bonnet, front grill, headlights and bumper. Meanwhile, in Guildford, tracker Richard is searching for a digger that’s been hidden on the edge of a golf course.

Gabby Logan leads the coverage and is joined in the studio by Jessica Ennis-Hill, Jenny Meadows and Greg Rutherford, with Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe in commentary.

programme.title: UEFA Champions League
programme.desc: Europa League winners Aston Villa take on Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain in the UEFA Super Cup in Salzburg. Villa won the Super Cup trophy on their only previous appearance, beating Barcelona over two legs back in 1982. PSG are the current holders after coming from 2-0 down to secure victory over Tottenham on penalties last year.

programme.title: Red Eye
programme.desc: A hotel manager's life is turned upside down when the enigmatic stranger in the seat next to her on a flight home demands her co-operation in a plot to assassinate a government official. If she refuses, her own father's life could be at stake.

programme.title: The Hit List

Taking on the musical challenge are presenter Chris Hughes and actor Jack P Shepherd, comedians Sara Pascoe and Rhys James, and actors Gary Lamont and Renee Bailey. Who will hit the high notes and who will fall flat? Get ready to play along!

programme.title: Black Black Oil
programme.desc: Documentary exploring our economic, historical and emotional entanglement with North Sea oil, which is getting evermore complex as we hurtle towards climate breakdown.

programme.title: River City
programme.desc: Things take a terrifying turn when Tommy collapses after being diagnosed with concussion. A dejected Tyler is forced to contemplate his next moves with Harry, Amber’s attempts at a grand gesture to Angus are interrupted by Teddy, and Chris tells Bob who he thinks Scarlett’s tormentor is.

programme.title: Icons of Football
programme.desc: Gary McAllister made the game of football look easy. The proverbial classy midfield player who saw the full picture, and could affect it, in the crucial seconds before his opponent. Unprepared to succumb to a story that began with knock-backs, Gary wrote his own place in the history and folklore of every club he played for - a winner at Motherwell, champion at Leeds, immortal at Liverpool, and a Scotland captain of some repute. But there were lows to counter the highs, and Gary discusses these with searing honesty. However, he is not defined by the hard times, but rather the moments where his class and will to win elevated him to the very top of the game. With contributions from Steven Gerrard, Gordon Strachan and Ardal O’Hanlon, this is the story of one of the greatest Scotland players of his, or any, generation.

programme.title: Scotcast
programme.desc: Conversation about Scotland’s biggest news stories, hosted by Martin Geissler.

programme.title: The Trials That Shocked Scotland
programme.desc: Through testimony, interviews and archive footage, this series examines high-profile court cases that have shocked Scotland. This episode features a family’s 18-year fight for justice following the 1998 murder of Surjit Singh Chhokar in Overtown. There is also the 2015 trial of William Paterson at the High Court in Glasgow. Paterson stood accused of shooting to death a well-known gangland figure in a busy supermarket car park five years earlier.

programme.title: Stacey Dooley
programme.desc: Stacey follows three Ukrainian civilians training with British soldiers to fight Russia. In just five weeks, a florist, a welder and a jeweller learn to 'survive and be lethal'.

programme.title: My Mate's a Bad Date
programme.desc: Twenty-five-year-old Mancunian Tyler is a self-confessed serial dater who treats dating like a sport and goes on five or six dates a week. She’s rude and sarcastic, rambles on about herself, gets bored easily and doesn’t stay focused on her dates. Best mate Yazmine is sick of hearing about Tyler’s dating disasters. Tyler needs help, so Yazmine calls on Gen Z’s most trusted sex and relationships expert, Oloni, to kick-start an intervention. Oloni pulls Tyler up on her catastrophic dating habits and delivers some tough truths as she and Tyler watch frank video feedback from friends and exes to prove to Tyler that there needs to be a change. Oloni has her job cut out with this one and sets Tyler up on three challenge dates as she and Yazmine watch on. Tyler insists her ideal date is the male version of herself, but will the male ‘Tyler’ be the perfect match for this feisty female?

programme.title: Stacey Dooley
programme.desc: Stacey Dooley’s first appearance on TV, in the iconic series about the true cost of fashion, first broadcast in 2008. Six young fashion lovers swap shopping for the factories and backstreet workshops of India to learn how the clothes they wear are manufactured. They start at the top, working for Shahi Enterprises in New Delhi, a multi-million pound factory that makes clothes for some of the biggest UK high street names. They learn to sew before joining the production lines where every worker has targets to meet. Supervisors patrol the lines and, at lunch, the sexes are made to sit apart. As unskilled workers they're paid around one pound fifty a day, a basic living wage in India.

programme.desc: This Country is a sitcom series for BBC Three which takes the mockumentary format to explore the lives of young people in modern rural Britain, focusing on cousins Kerry and Lee ‘Kurtan’ Mucklowe and their life experiences in a typical Cotswold village. programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: In Greater Manchester, upcycling expert Jacqui Joseph explores the Altrincham recycling centre, hoping to discover unwanted items that can be revamped or revitalised and sold on for cash. She calls on lighting designer Duncan to restore a once-loved retro radio, and can newbie Tyler find a way to save an old sewing machine table?

programme.title: Great Japanese Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael’s bullet train takes him through the undersea Seikan tunnel to Hokkaido, the most northerly of Japan’s main islands and home to the indigenous Ainu people. He begins by exploring the southern city of Hakodate, one of the ports which was first to trade with the outside world. Visiting a family-run miso factory, he finds out how the staple Japanese ingredient is made using soybeans and a cultured mould known as koji. In the centre of the city, Michael visits the star-shaped Fort Goryokaku, the setting for a turning point in Japanese history. He discovers how the last remnants of the Tokugawa military forces were defeated in 1869 by the new Emperor Meiji’s army, ushering in a new modern era for Japan. Swapping the Shinkansen for a slower pace in a diesel train, Michael leaves the city to explore Hokkaido’s stunning volcanic landscape, travelling to Lake Toya in the Shikotsu-Toya National Park.

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway journey through the islands of Sardinia and Corsica sees him leave Sardinia and arrive into Corsica, the most mountainous island in the Mediterranean. In Ajaccio, he delves into the early life of the island’s most famous son, Napoleon Bonaparte, discovering how Corsica’s unique approach to childhood shaped the future conqueror. At a bustling food market, Michael samples the island’s wild herbs. He is captivated by the haunting harmonies of polyphonic singing, a sound deeply woven into the island’s soul. He then boards the legendary Trinichellu, Corsica’s historic metre-gauge mountain railway, for a breathtaking journey through the island’s rugged interior. In the heart of the wilderness, Michael discovers how cutting-edge technology and drones are being used in the battle against devastating wildfires, a crucial innovation protecting Corsica and beyond.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Margie Cooper v Tim Medhurst, round three, as they hop over the English border to the green grass of Wales in their electric green fire engine. They head to the home of the famous Ladies of Llangollen and take some tasty treats to auction. But will their offerings go down well?

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Developers in Eye in Cambridgeshire and Hylton Castle near Sunderland rejig layouts in their two-bedroom houses to create an additional bedroom for each home, while developers in Ramsgate in Kent turn their three-bedroom house into a two-bedder in favour of a stunning large bathroom. But will their decisions make them money?

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: The market town of Leominster is the destination for today’s show. Guiding the teams around an antiques centre in the Herefordshire town are Kate Bliss and Philip Serrell, but which team will make the biggest profit or the smallest loss at auction? Meanwhile, presenter Eric Knowles visits Hereford Cathedral’s 17th-century library, where the books are kept under lock and key.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Mehreen Baig, Clare Balding, Jamie Laing and Mike Wozniak take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted by the House of Games reusable coffee mug, which is brand new for this series?

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and his sidekick Sarah Greene host this quiz show, where the contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races, where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: Celebrity players Nitin Ganatra, the Rev Kate Bottley and Alex Gray, aka Apollo from Gladiators, face another knowledge battle, led by Vernon Kay and aided by unreliable tour guide Paul Gorton. It's the halfway point, and the gloves are off for today’s destination, Falkirk.

programme.title: The Farmers' Country Showdown
programme.desc: Goat breeders Sam and Jess are excited to have a day away from their Sheffield smallholding and head to the Royal Cheshire County Show with their beloved goat herd in tow. A lot rides on today’s results, including whether their male goat Apollo becomes a champion winner this year. Meanwhile, goat farming couple Mark and Graeme from Catterick have been monitoring milk yields and ensuring their pedigree herd is in top condition for the competition. Devoted to his goats, Mark hopes a perfect performance will be rewarded with the very best rosettes.

programme.title: Spy in the Ocean
programme.desc: Spy creatures uncover surprising undersea relationships as sharks befriend fish, whales play with dolphins, and lobsters do the conga in seas where even spider crabs have friends.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: In the second visit to Sherborne School in Dorset, Michael Aspel and the experts find an original monk's bench, letters from Lewis Carroll and an 18th-century satinwood cabinet of great value, as well as a 'naughty' cigarette case and part of the airframe of the R100 airship.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: The show comes from the RAF Museum at Hendon in London. Antiques experts Anita Manning and Mark Stacey find some real treasures among the bags and boxes to take to auction. There's a photo album of RAF Hendon in the 30s and a rare picture that brings a surprise in the saleroom. And Paul Martin visits an exhibition of First World War flying pioneers.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Chris Bisson, Danielle Harold, Katharine Merry and Robert Webb take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games retro bag?

programme.title: Bear Grylls - Wild Reckoning
programme.desc: Estranged brother and sister Dawn and David come face to face for the first time in nearly five years. Their relationship has always been complicated, with Dawn being given up for adoption at birth while her younger brother was kept. Dawn reconnected with the family in her teens but struggled to feel accepted. When she failed to attend their birth mother’s funeral, David broke off contact. The pair take on a navigation challenge and, the ultimate test of trust, a counterbalance abseil. They also confront painful subjects from their past in an emotional campfire chat with relationship therapist Simone. Will two days surviving in the wild be enough to heal the rift between them?

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: The men’s decathlon continues on day three of the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham with the high jump and the 400m. A new champion will also be crowned as the women’s hammer final gets underway. Gabby Logan is joined in the studio by Jessica Ennis-Hill, Jenny Meadows and Greg Rutherford, and they also reflect on all the action from the morning session. Commentary comes from Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc: The team restores a photo of President Kennedy’s children with their English nanny, a tiny drum kit clock, a melted wax statuette and a traditional Venezuelan stringed instrument.

programme.title: Murder Trial
programme.desc: In 2024, the body of 65-year-old groundsman Brian Low is discovered on a country track in rural Aberfeldy, his beloved black labrador Millie by his side. Police assume that Brian has suffered a medical episode, but six days later, the post-mortem reveals the shocking truth - Brian has been shot dead. His former colleague and gamekeeper on the estate where he worked, David Campbell, now stands trial for his murder. With the site of the murder exposed to the elements for days, police are unable to forensically link anyone to the deceased. The prosecution builds a case against the accused around smaller, individual strands of circumstantial evidence while working to convince the jury that he is guilty beyond reasonable doubt.

programme.title: Inside No. 9
programme.desc: Shane and Clifford have a plan to abduct the wife of a wealthy hedge fund manager. If he won’t pay them the money, they’ll snip her ears off to prove they mean business. Everything in the plan depends on everyone playing their part right to the end. It’s totally foolproof - isn’t it?

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Katie Razzall.

programme.title: Evolution
programme.desc: How did the horse become so fast? Chris Packham sets out on a slithering, swimming, sprinting odyssey that explores the evolutionary beginnings of animal movement and how it reached its peak in one of the most elegant and athletic animals on earth: the horse.

programme.title: Kindling
programme.desc: A group of young men return to their home town in order to turn their friend's final days into a celebration of life and friendship.

In Ajaccio, he delves into the early life of the island’s most famous son, Napoleon Bonaparte, discovering how Corsica’s unique approach to childhood shaped the future conqueror. At a bustling food market, Michael samples the island’s wild herbs. He is captivated by the haunting harmonies of polyphonic singing, a sound deeply woven into the island’s soul. He then boards the legendary Trinichellu, Corsica’s historic metre-gauge mountain railway, for a breathtaking journey through the island’s rugged interior. In the heart of the wilderness, Michael discovers how cutting-edge technology and drones are being used in the battle against devastating wildfires, a crucial innovation protecting Corsica and beyond.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Margie Cooper v Tim Medhurst, round three, as they hop over the English border to the green grass of Wales in their electric green fire engine. They head to the home of the famous Ladies of Llangollen and take some tasty treats to auction. But will their offerings go down well?

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Developers in Eye in Cambridgeshire and Hylton Castle near Sunderland rejig layouts in their two-bedroom houses to create an additional bedroom for each home, while developers in Ramsgate in Kent turn their three-bedroom house into a two-bedder in favour of a stunning large bathroom. But will their decisions make them money?

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: The market town of Leominster is the destination for today’s show. Guiding the teams around an antiques centre in the Herefordshire town are Kate Bliss and Philip Serrell, but which team will make the biggest profit or the smallest loss at auction? Meanwhile, presenter Eric Knowles visits Hereford Cathedral’s 17th-century library, where the books are kept under lock and key.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Mehreen Baig, Clare Balding, Jamie Laing and Mike Wozniak take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted by the House of Games reusable coffee mug, which is brand new for this series?

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and his sidekick Sarah Greene host this quiz show, where the contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races, where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: Celebrity players Nitin Ganatra, the Rev Kate Bottley and Alex Gray, aka Apollo from Gladiators, face another knowledge battle, led by Vernon Kay and aided by unreliable tour guide Paul Gorton. It's the halfway point, and the gloves are off for today’s destination, Falkirk.

programme.title: The Farmers' Country Showdown
programme.desc: Goat breeders Sam and Jess are excited to have a day away from their Sheffield smallholding and head to the Royal Cheshire County Show with their beloved goat herd in tow. A lot rides on today’s results, including whether their male goat Apollo becomes a champion winner this year. Meanwhile, goat farming couple Mark and Graeme from Catterick have been monitoring milk yields and ensuring their pedigree herd is in top condition for the competition. Devoted to his goats, Mark hopes a perfect performance will be rewarded with the very best rosettes.

programme.title: Spy in the Ocean
programme.desc: Spy creatures uncover surprising undersea relationships as sharks befriend fish, whales play with dolphins, and lobsters do the conga in seas where even spider crabs have friends.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: In the second visit to Sherborne School in Dorset, Michael Aspel and the experts find an original monk's bench, letters from Lewis Carroll and an 18th-century satinwood cabinet of great value, as well as a 'naughty' cigarette case and part of the airframe of the R100 airship.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: The show comes from the RAF Museum at Hendon in London. Antiques experts Anita Manning and Mark Stacey find some real treasures among the bags and boxes to take to auction. There's a photo album of RAF Hendon in the 30s and a rare picture that brings a surprise in the saleroom. And Paul Martin visits an exhibition of First World War flying pioneers.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Chris Bisson, Danielle Harold, Katharine Merry and Robert Webb take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games retro bag?

programme.title: Bear Grylls - Wild Reckoning
programme.desc: Estranged brother and sister Dawn and David come face to face for the first time in nearly five years. Their relationship has always been complicated, with Dawn being given up for adoption at birth while her younger brother was kept. Dawn reconnected with the family in her teens but struggled to feel accepted. When she failed to attend their birth mother’s funeral, David broke off contact. The pair take on a navigation challenge and, the ultimate test of trust, a counterbalance abseil. They also confront painful subjects from their past in an emotional campfire chat with relationship therapist Simone. Will two days surviving in the wild be enough to heal the rift between them?

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: The men’s decathlon continues on day three of the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham with the high jump and the 400m. A new champion will also be crowned as the women’s hammer final gets underway. Gabby Logan is joined in the studio by Jessica Ennis-Hill, Jenny Meadows and Greg Rutherford, and they also reflect on all the action from the morning session. Commentary comes from Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc: The team restores a photo of President Kennedy’s children with their English nanny, a tiny drum kit clock, a melted wax statuette and a traditional Venezuelan stringed instrument.

programme.title: Murder Trial
programme.desc: In 2024, the body of 65-year-old groundsman Brian Low is discovered on a country track in rural Aberfeldy, his beloved black labrador Millie by his side. Police assume that Brian has suffered a medical episode, but six days later, the post-mortem reveals the shocking truth - Brian has been shot dead. His former colleague and gamekeeper on the estate where he worked, David Campbell, now stands trial for his murder. With the site of the murder exposed to the elements for days, police are unable to forensically link anyone to the deceased. The prosecution builds a case against the accused around smaller, individual strands of circumstantial evidence while working to convince the jury that he is guilty beyond reasonable doubt.

programme.title: Inside No. 9
programme.desc: Shane and Clifford have a plan to abduct the wife of a wealthy hedge fund manager. If he won’t pay them the money, they’ll snip her ears off to prove they mean business. Everything in the plan depends on everyone playing their part right to the end. It’s totally foolproof - isn’t it?

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Katie Razzall.

programme.title: Evolution
programme.desc: How did the horse become so fast? Chris Packham sets out on a slithering, swimming, sprinting odyssey that explores the evolutionary beginnings of animal movement and how it reached its peak in one of the most elegant and athletic animals on earth: the horse.

programme.title: Kindling
programme.desc: A group of young men return to their home town in order to turn their friend's final days into a celebration of life and friendship.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: In Greater Manchester, upcycling expert Jacqui Joseph explores the Altrincham recycling centre, hoping to discover unwanted items that can be revamped or revitalised and sold on for cash. She calls on lighting designer Duncan to restore a once-loved retro radio, and can newbie Tyler find a way to save an old sewing machine table?

programme.title: Great Japanese Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael’s bullet train takes him through the undersea Seikan tunnel to Hokkaido, the most northerly of Japan’s main islands and home to the indigenous Ainu people. He begins by exploring the southern city of Hakodate, one of the ports which was first to trade with the outside world. Visiting a family-run miso factory, he finds out how the staple Japanese ingredient is made using soybeans and a cultured mould known as koji. In the centre of the city, Michael visits the star-shaped Fort Goryokaku, the setting for a turning point in Japanese history. He discovers how the last remnants of the Tokugawa military forces were defeated in 1869 by the new Emperor Meiji’s army, ushering in a new modern era for Japan. Swapping the Shinkansen for a slower pace in a diesel train, Michael leaves the city to explore Hokkaido’s stunning volcanic landscape, travelling to Lake Toya in the Shikotsu-Toya National Park.

programme.desc: Estranged brother and sister Dawn and David come face to face for the first time in nearly five years. Their relationship has always been complicated, with Dawn being given up for adoption at birth while her younger brother was kept. programme.title: Murder Trial
programme.desc: In 2024, the body of 65-year-old groundsman Brian Low is discovered on a country track in rural Aberfeldy, his beloved black labrador Millie by his side. Police assume that Brian has suffered a medical episode, but six days later, the post-mortem reveals the shocking truth - Brian has been shot dead. His former colleague and gamekeeper on the estate where he worked, David Campbell, now stands trial for his murder. With the site of the murder exposed to the elements for days, police are unable to forensically link anyone to the deceased. The prosecution builds a case against the accused around smaller, individual strands of circumstantial evidence while working to convince the jury that he is guilty beyond reasonable doubt.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: In Greater Manchester, upcycling expert Jacqui Joseph explores the Altrincham recycling centre, hoping to discover unwanted items that can be revamped or revitalised and sold on for cash. She calls on lighting designer Duncan to restore a once-loved retro radio, and can newbie Tyler find a way to save an old sewing machine table?

programme.title: Great Japanese Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael’s bullet train takes him through the undersea Seikan tunnel to Hokkaido, the most northerly of Japan’s main islands and home to the indigenous Ainu people. He begins by exploring the southern city of Hakodate, one of the ports which was first to trade with the outside world. Visiting a family-run miso factory, he finds out how the staple Japanese ingredient is made using soybeans and a cultured mould known as koji. In the centre of the city, Michael visits the star-shaped Fort Goryokaku, the setting for a turning point in Japanese history. He discovers how the last remnants of the Tokugawa military forces were defeated in 1869 by the new Emperor Meiji’s army, ushering in a new modern era for Japan. Swapping the Shinkansen for a slower pace in a diesel train, Michael leaves the city to explore Hokkaido’s stunning volcanic landscape, travelling to Lake Toya in the Shikotsu-Toya National Park.

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway journey through the islands of Sardinia and Corsica sees him leave Sardinia and arrive into Corsica, the most mountainous island in the Mediterranean. In Ajaccio, he delves into the early life of the island’s most famous son, Napoleon Bonaparte, discovering how Corsica’s unique approach to childhood shaped the future conqueror. At a bustling food market, Michael samples the island’s wild herbs. He is captivated by the haunting harmonies of polyphonic singing, a sound deeply woven into the island’s soul. He then boards the legendary Trinichellu, Corsica’s historic metre-gauge mountain railway, for a breathtaking journey through the island’s rugged interior. In the heart of the wilderness, Michael discovers how cutting-edge technology and drones are being used in the battle against devastating wildfires, a crucial innovation protecting Corsica and beyond.

programme.title: Pokémon Horizons

programme.desc: Adam and Rocco take on Joe and Otis to find out which human makes the best hound. A test of agility, smell and teamwork - only one furry duo will win!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Animated preschool series. Duggee is sewing a snazzy poncho, and the Squirrels want to make one too. programme.title: Bluey

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: The Go Jetters travel to the Valley of Balls in Kazakhstan, where they find thousands of rocks which are almost perfectly round. The Go Jetters take to the Vroomster to try to stop the ball.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit

programme.title: Octonauts

programme.title: Numberblocks

programme.title: Alphablocks

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: The Piripenguins fall under the spell of a magical Merguin, a mermaid-penguin, who has the ability to change their personality. But all is not as it seems.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: Gadabout and Pearl need Zog's help to catch a stink beetle for an urgent cure. Little do they know, Zog has become a taxi for the gnomes.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Mojo and Bo join the big cross-town race with plans to win. But how can they stay ahead when they have to keep stopping and swopping to help other racers in trouble?

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing and Sula are painting in the garden. When Bing cleans his brush and accidentally knocks the water over, he goes to fill it up from the garden tap. But he turns the water on too fast, making the hose voosh up into a big snake of water that covers Bing and Sula in wet paint! Flop shows Bing how to turn the tap on slowly.

programme.title: Yakka Dee!
programme.desc: Dee encourages a friend to say ‘alien’, and we go on a whirlwind word adventure. We meet lots of different aliens – a green alien with feelers from outer space, a quick one and an alien doing a trick. Dee tries to find a hiding alien, and then Dee and a friend see aliens with different numbers of eyes. The journey is repeated with some special surprises along the way, and everyone has a boogie when Dee’s friend finally succeeds in saying today’s word.

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Maddie, Triggs, Mum and Dad are going for a walk in the countryside, but Dad is adamant that he does not want his pristine hiking shoes to get dirty. Luckily, Maddie and Triggs are on hand to stop their buddy getting muddy!

programme.title: Piggy Builders
programme.desc: Cherry dreams of soaring through the sky. The Piggy Builders build her a plane, but she jumps in without learning how to fly. Taking off is easy, but landing? A disaster! Cherry thinks flying isn’t for her, but for the Piggies won't give up.

programme.title: Twirlywoos
programme.desc: The Twirlywoos watch a man whose car is stuck in the mud. The man tries pulling the car free with a rope but it won't budge. When the man goes off to phone for help, the Twirlywoos step in and try pulling the car out of the mud themselves. Chickedy and Chick try pulling, then Toodloo tries pulling, but the car is still stuck. Finally, when all the Twirlywoos work together they manage to pull the car out of the mud!

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Justin and his friend head to a marina for lots of boating fun. Meanwhile, Mr Tumble has ordered a new inflatable boat to take fishing. What could possibly go wrong?

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Tinky Winky's bag fills up with sparkles from a tap, and when Home Dome overflows with tubby custard, Po has to turn the Tubby Custard Machine off. A child in Tummy Tales uses a new tap in the bathroom when she brushes her teeth before bedtime.

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Giovanna and Baby Bear welcome babies Roman, Rose-May, Zachary, Thomas, Finley, Ferne and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Parents, carers and their babies at home are invited to join in with all the fun activities too! In this episode we meet a new friend, Baby Tiger. There are scarves inside everyone’s bags which are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding baby appropriate scarves inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby! The baby song Scarves Are Waving! features, as does a story involving Baby Bear. Plus, the Action Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: I Spy, You Spy
programme.desc: Elsee plays I-spy whilst on a bus adventure with her new friend Chase.

programme.title: What’s in Your Plant Pot?
programme.desc: Farmer Alisha introduces the Fact Pack to mushrooms. They discover that mushrooms are fungi, how they grow from mycelium and why some have very different flavours.

programme.title: Let's Go for a Walk
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers walk through the forest to make some bark rubbings. On the way, they see a rainbow shaped tree, discover a secret passage, play a game of Three Little Pigs and even visit a bug hotel!

programme.title: Kiri and Lou
programme.desc: Kiri meets a little dinosaur who has lost her way.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey and Bingo want a pet. To show them how much work they'd be in for, Dad gets to transform his hand into their old friend Shaun, a chaotic, undisciplined Emu with a taste for trouble.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels help Duggee try out his new outdoor pizza oven. Duggee makes the bases, then the Squirrels each put on all the toppings they like best. Some of their combinations are... interesting!

programme.title: Teeny Tiny Creatures
programme.desc: Holly wants to know all there is to know about wriggly earthworms! Ferne visits a worm farm and meets worm expert Ken, and they handle different species of UK worms. Meanwhile, Rory and his son Sandy search the compost bin and the garden for worms and decide to build a wormery to make worm tea! Also, we find out why earthworms are so important to the planet by being amazing soil engineers.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Sisters Kyra and Khloe go on a big family day out to a farm. There are lots of exciting things to do, including a pony ride, or should that be a unicorn ride? They explore an amazing maze where the girls find a giant sunflower! But will they ever find their way back out? They also discover a very muddy and squelchy pumpkin patch and pick their perfect pumpkins! This Bafta-winning pre-school observational documentary follows the lives of young children and their families from a variety of backgrounds across the UK.

programme.title: Big Cook Little Cook
programme.desc: It’s treat time in the cafe today, and the chefs want to eat ice cream, but the freezer is too cold to go near. Walter Wizard visits them, Small flies off to see how beetroot grows, and the two friends whisk up cauldron soup for their magical guest.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Guide dog Kika and her owner Dr Amit are off to the Sticks 'n’ Stuff shop with Amit’s friend Alana, who is also blind, to help her buy a new white cane.

programme.title: Time for School
programme.desc: The class arrives wearing brightly coloured clothes for a fun-filled activity day. There’s a colourful science experiment and a colour safari adventure around the school.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Evie and Waffle arrive home from school with Gramps for a playdate with Ruby and her dog, Jelly. Just as they’re all about to go inside the house, a delivery van arrives with shopping for Mrs Hobbs, next door.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Isabelle and Oona are in a rush today - they are running to the beach to catch a glimpse of a cattle egret. Oona has never seen one before, but Isabelle knows that they're big! While the others hurry along, Baba discovers a whole new small world along the way. Sometimes, it's good to slow down and see the small things - as well as the big ones.

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: The garden gang are intrigued when Yukee says she’s going to stay up late with them so that she can show them the Man in the Moon. But will they all be able to stay awake long enough to see him?

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: While out for an evening walk, Maddie, Triggs and Dad meet a little bat who's lost! As Brigid tells them all about how she uses sound to get around, Maddie and Triggs make some bat noises of their own as they take flight and help Brigid find her way back home.

programme.title: Piggy Builders
programme.desc: Wilf wants a new hobby, so the Piggies suggest golf. But when he and Cornelia compete to see who can hit the ball the farthest, they start breaking things. Cesar and Charlie must find a way to get them to play more gently!

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: New Numberblock Nineteen discovers she's a one-off with a hidden talent for shape-shifting. Learn all about the number 19 with Numberblock Nineteen!

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: Educational fun. The adventures of 26 lively letters who can make words come to life by holding hands. It's pandemonium at the Alphablocks' animal singsong. S has a special surprise in store. This episode has fun with the words cat, dog, cod, tag, jog, jig, mop, moo, moon, spoon and zoom.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Educational series using Makaton sign language. Justin and his friends go for a haircut today, while Mr Tumble has lots of messy fun pretending to be a hairdresser.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: After a fun waving game with the Tiddlytubbies, the Teletubbies enjoy watching children waving as they set off on a short boat trip. Finally, the Teletubbies wave to the Tiddlytubbies, who are off to sleepybyes.

programme.title: Hamza Loves Animals: Africa
programme.desc: Kipekee the baby elephant is fed up with being small. Hamza finds some wonderful wildebeest in the wild. Later, he uses a brush to help the baby rhinos relax.

programme.title: Molly and Mack
programme.desc: Molly examines her shelf of special things at the back of Mack’s stall. She chooses the squidgy magic ball and remembers the day she got it. Mack is helping Kez with her boxes, but Moira says they need to be moved out of the way. Kez tries to distract her with a magic trick, but Moira insists the boxes need to be gone. At the Kids Club, Caitlin is trying to do a magic trick with Euan, but her disappearing-the-ball trick doesn’t quite work. Ayesha arrives and does the trick properly, using the magic words ‘mish mash mosh’. Caitlin decides they’re not going to play magic anymore. Instead, they will play a game. She decides that Ayesha and Euan can play castle guards who don’t speak. Mack suggests to Kez that they use the boxes to help Caitlin with her game, and she creates an amazing castle. When Caitlin arrives at the gate, she finds she can’t get in without a password. Euan and Ayesha know the password but can’t reveal it as they’re not allowed to speak. Caitlin and Ayesha need to work together to figure it out. Later, Moira is pleased to see the boxes have gone but has to laugh when she finds where Mack and Kez have put them.

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: In this bumpy and muddy episode, CBeebies' very own motorbike rider Grace shows off three amazing machines that are all made to go off-road! Grace drives the funny spider car, shows off the daring Formula Off-Road buggies and goes for a drive in an eight-wheeled all-terrain vehicle!

programme.title: Dodge's Pup School
programme.desc: Dodge is determined to win the Class Star award, but with Cherry winning every week for being a superstar at everything, it’s going to be tough! Dodge, Woofer and Jazz try to hatch a plan, but when Jazz and Dodge get swept up in their ideas, like getting Miss Collie a gift, they ignore Woofer’s advice that there’s a better way. Dodge brings Miss Collie a gift into the classroom from the playground and chaos ensues, leaving Dodge with no hope of winning the class star. Dodge discovers that the real key to winning is by trying his best.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger must navigate chaos amid rolling Coconutdons and tail-swatting Pineapplesauruses.

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond
programme.desc: When the underwater Kavachi volcano erupts, Ryla calls on the Octonauts to help.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: Cheeky Peter Rabbit loves adventure but he struggles to stay out of trouble. Luckily his best friends are always around to help him out. Based on Beatrix Potter's classic stories.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Join Duggee, a big, lovable dog, as he runs the Squirrel Club, where children can earn badges for learning new skills. Warm-hearted preschool series about trying new things.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: When Koa gets stung by a bee, Vida helps him get over his fear and make a new friend.

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: Carrot is excited to show the Tato Team her new inventions, including an improved Robotato, who will help them protect the supermarket from Evil Pea. Unfortunately, Robotato still has a few glitches, so the veggies decide to test Carrot's new jetpacks instead, but Evil Pea sneaks in and commands Robotato to protect her. When Robotato continues to glitch, he becomes overly protective of Evil Pea and takes her to the top of Tato Tower to keep her safe. The Tato Team, led by the real Supertato, must use their new jetpacks to fly up and save her.

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: The ducklings want to take a beautiful family portrait with their pop, but Weasy can’t help making faces and monkeying around. The ducklings decide to take a surprise photo of him so that he’ll look natural.

programme.title: Do Not Watch This Show
programme.desc: A mysterious bucket floats over Wizz's head and will tip over if you keep watching.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Judo wants to play in the dirt with Bluey and Bingo, but she’s not supposed to get dirty!

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Mum bans the girls from saying 'dunny', so they try and trick her into saying it instead.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: Pearl accidentally gives Fizz and Zog a laughing disease called the draggles. The doctors must create an emotion potion before every dragon chuckles themselves to exhaustion.

programme.title: Andy's Dino Island
programme.desc: When Jen is carried away by a weather balloon, Andy sets out on an epic adventure across Dino Island to rescue her. Along the way, they meet the mighty Alamosaurus, a gigantic dinosaur that's as long as two double-decker buses! It comes to their aid when they get trapped on an island by an ancient crocodilian, called Deinosuchus, lurking in the surrounding waters.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is an adorable talking dog who can't help but cause trouble! His everyday adventures are full of mayhem and mischief. Warning: theme tune guaranteed to stick in your head.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi promises her dads she will go straight to bed while Aunty T babysits. But when Aunty T suggests night-time ice cream, Rafi makes a wish and her bed magically flies them out into Manchester! It’s exciting at first, but soon Rafi becomes sleepy and wants to go home. Suddenly, the wish runs out and the bed drops onto a tree. Luckily, Aunty T uses her umbrella to magic them safely back. Rafi realises bedtime is bedtime for a reason.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: JoJo and Gran Gran are on a day trip to the sunny seaside with one mission in mind: to build the biggest sandcastle ever built so that Panda can play inside. But JoJo has no luck with building her sandcastle and feels disheartened when she learns about the tide and how it will carry her best sandcastle yet away into the sea! But with Gran Gran on hand, JoJo learns that things don't need to last forever to be special as the pair take lots of pictures for them to keep forever and remember.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Bug and his friends lead Sarah and Duck to their outdoor music concert.

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: When he and Small look through the telescope, they see just the place - a golden planet. Unfortunately Tiny discovers that the golden planet they see is not what it appears to be.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa are having a race, but BaBa always starts before Gramma Leeba says go, never waiting. At Play Time, BaBa knocks down MeMo’s brick tower before it has been built. MeMo and the Yummies encourage BaBa to wait for the snacks to be ready before trying to eat them. BaBa waits - and they're delicious! On the Lullaby Lake, BaBa has learned to wait and is rewarded with a beautiful performance.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: After waking Upsy Daisy, Igglepiggle goes with her for a walk in the garden. Upsy Daisy's bed decides to follow them even when they ride on the Ninky Nonk. When Upsy Daisy decides she would like a rest, her bed makes her chase after it.

programme.title: CBeebies Bedtime Stories
programme.desc: This story is about a boy and a dog that make the perfect pair. Mr Scruff is a sweet story about unlikely friendships, read by Rick Astley.
